title: L.N. Mattei Cap Corse Rouge
about: Louis-Napoléon Mattei was born in 1849 in Ersa, at the northern tip of Cap Corse, the narrow peninsula that runs north from Bastia. As a young man he kept a shop in Bastia selling coffee, tobacco, wine and liqueurs, and in the early 1870s he began distilling Corsican cédrat, the thick-skinned citron of the cape, into his own liqueurs. The house counts 1872 as its founding year, and its shop on Bastia’s Place Saint-Nicolas is now a listed historic monument. Its importer notes that the house still carries out its own macerations, ageing and bottling.

Cap Corse is a quinquina, an aperitif wine built on cinchona bark, the source of quinine. Its base is a mistelle: fresh Muscat and Vermentinu grape must from the north of the island, its fermentation stopped with neutral alcohol so that the grapes’ own sugar remains and no sweetener is added. Into the Rouge go macerations of cinchona bark and local cédrat, along with aromatic spices and walnuts (the label notes that it contains nuts). It is bottled at 17% alcohol.

The Rouge pours a coppery amber rather than a true red. Quinine bitterness and white-grape acidity meet a honeyed, caramel sweetness, with rosemary and other herbs in the middle and a long, notably dry finish. Across Corsica it is poured in bars as the Capo Spritz; traditionally it is taken neat over ice or lengthened with tonic or soda and a twist of orange or other citrus peel; its importer suggests it also pairs well with rye whiskey, apple brandy or brandy in cocktails.
facts: Mistelle of Corsican Muscat and Vermentinu
Cinchona bark, cédrat (citron), aromatic spices, walnuts
Over ice, neat or with tonic and orange peel
